name: Rabbit
intro: A rabbit is a small, furry mammal with long ears. It can hop and jump.

sections.title: What does it look like?
sentences: A rabbit has fur and long ears.
Its ears can turn to hear sounds.
Its eyes are on the sides of its head.
It can see almost all the way around.
Its front teeth never stop growing.

sections.title: Where does it live?
sentences: Rabbits live in meadows, woods, and grasslands.
Some live in deserts and wetlands.
Many rabbits live in holes called burrows.
A group of burrows is called a warren.
Cottontail rabbits live in yards and on farms.

sections.title: What does it eat?
sentences: Rabbits eat plants.
They eat grass, clover, and dandelions.
Chewing wears down their growing teeth.
Rabbits sometimes nibble tree bark.
Carrots are not a natural rabbit food.

sections.title: How does it grow?
sentences: A baby rabbit is called a kit.
A mother rabbit makes a nest of grass and fur.
Kits are born with no fur, and they cannot see.
A mother can have many kits at one time.
Cottontail kits leave the nest after about two weeks.

sections.title: Fun facts
sentences: A happy rabbit does a twisty jump called a binky.
Happy rabbits can purr like cats.
A rabbit can jump higher than a kitchen table.
A girl rabbit is a doe, and a boy is a buck.
Cottontails are busy from evening to early morning.

vocab.meaning: An animal with fur that feeds its babies milk.
